what_it_is.prose: Dhaksha Unmanned Systems is a Chennai-based UAV OEM incorporated in 2019, manufacturing hybrid petrol-engine and battery-electric drones for defence, agriculture and enterprise. It won the Indian Air Force's Mehar Baba Swarm Drone Competition (2021), secured a 200-unit logistics drone order from the Indian Army (later put on hold over Chinese-parts concerns in 2024), and a 400-unit agricultural drone order from IFFCO. Dhaksha was among the first Indian companies to receive DGCA type certification for an IC-engine agriculture drone (AgriGator, Oct 2022). The company is a strategic partner to MIT-Anna University.

faq.question: What major Indian Army order did Dhaksha Unmanned Systems receive and what was its status?
faq.answer: Dhaksha received a ₹165 crore Indian Army order for 200 medium-altitude logistics drones and accessories. In August 2024, the Indian Army put the purchase on hold over concerns about Chinese components in the drones.

faq.question: Which DGCA type-certified agriculture drone does Dhaksha manufacture?
faq.answer: Dhaksha's AgriGator (DH-AG-H1) is India's only medium-category IC-engine agriculture drone and was DGCA Type Certified in October 2022. It features a 12-litre spray tank.

faq.question: What is Dhaksha's connection to the IAF Mehar Baba Swarm Drone Competition?
faq.answer: Dhaksha won the 2021 Indian Air Force Mehar Baba Swarm Drone Competition, outperforming 154 competitors. The competition was launched by the IAF in October 2018 to stimulate swarm drone development.
